**Security: pass-with-notes** at `86f3499d3ad88e4b7eb58957448291d9ca388a19`, under C33/C34.

Packet-file expansion reads literal file/stdin content in the CLI and forwards one packet argument, without shell evaluation or a daemon-side caller-file read. Invalid-subject refusal uses a length-only rendering rather than echoing hostile input. No scoped vulnerability or demonstrated normal-use blocker was established.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No scoped security vulnerabilities found | - |

## Focused source checks

`file_flag_to_value` supports separate and `=` path forms, preserves arguments after `--`, refuses a missing value and propagates read failure before sending. The CLI reads `-` from stdin and other sources with `read_to_string`, relative to its working directory. File content is a JSON argv value for `--packet`, not shell syntax. Existing packet/brief validation remains in the daemon.

The new subject check trims the value and compares its closed renderer result. Nonmatching values are refused with shared accepted-form guidance and no raw subject content. Stored metadata also trims the subject. `file:<path>` is a subject label, not an instruction to read that file.

**C34 follow-up:** an exact invalid-label fixed point, such as `invalid (18 chars)`, can equal its own rendered result and pass the comparison despite lacking `<kind>:<name>`. This cannot inject framing; a grammar predicate would enforce the documented acceptance rule exactly. It is not a normal-use blocker.

File-read errors identify the selected path, not file contents. Their CLI path presentation remains raw for unusual filenames; no shell evaluation is involved. No new per-seat file isolation is required under C33.

Project help returns before client creation; shim help uses the same fixed text. Native verb forwarding and OMP routing are updated together. The generic edit-help form now supports the existing role-flag examples. No new authority or launch path was identified.

This implementation supplies the subject-refusal dependency for #209, but #209 must still merge after the bundle. No live inventory scan or claim of every possible file-path syntax is made.

## Evidence

The shared detached worktree is clean; local/remote/GitHub heads agree. CI [42577561325](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42577561325) succeeded on merge `3cafe0848dd404037e880095055fec93579d73fd`, with this head and main `f7744c5c3f677732af8b3c0a4dad657544811ce0` as parents; tree `c7f88ce01a575c78396fc4e21783c6b81a3dd3d9`.

JUnit artifact [13655474821](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42577561325/artifacts/13655474821) confirms 2,342 passing cases, no failures; six separately skipped. Offline project help, injected-read packet/stdin expansion, native-forwarding parity, edit-help and subject-refusal cases executed successfully. The packet test verifies the conversion with a supplied reader, not a live filesystem/stdin process probe.

The helper returned no assessment; supporting judgment rests on direct scoped source inspection and CI. No local builds/tests, credential reads, live-system probes or product edits.
